title: How Buffett owns businesses: 2020 letter on the PCC mistake, repurchases, float and partnership
summary: Buffett's 2020 letter owns up to overpaying for Precision Castparts, explains why non-controlling stakes in great businesses beat controlling marginal ones, and shows how disciplined buybacks and retained earnings compound value. It also covers float, ultra-low bond yields, and treating shareholders as partners.

principles.text: Own businesses by durable strengths, management and price; control is unimportant.
principles.quote: owning a non-controlling portion of a wonderful business is more profitable, more enjoyable and far less work than struggling with 100% of a marginal enterprise.

principles.text: Treat marketable stock holdings as businesses; unrecorded retained earnings build real value.
principles.quote: What’s out of sight, however, should not be out of mind: Those unrecorded retained earnings are usually building value – lots of value – for Berkshire.

principles.text: Admit mistakes plainly: he overpaid for PCC by misjudging future normalized earnings.
principles.quote: I was wrong, however, in judging the average amount of future earnings and, consequently, wrong in my calculation of the proper price to pay for the business.

principles.text: Repurchase only below intrinsic value; most CEOs buy back more when prices are high.
principles.quote: American CEOs have an embarrassing record of devoting more company funds to repurchases when prices have risen than when they have tanked. Our approach is exactly the reverse.

principles.text: Conglomerates fail by using overvalued stock to pay control premiums for mediocre businesses.
principles.quote: Most of the truly great businesses had no interest in having anyone take them over.

principles.text: Equity investing is positive-sum; patience, diversification and low fees win, and investor expenses are Wall Street's income.
principles.quote: All that’s required is the passage of time, an inner calm, ample diversification and a minimization of transactions and fees.
